name: FIELD-GUN19-1-the-muzzle-is-mapped-through-the-canvas-again
note: The bug itself: the docked large HUD shrinks the world pass, so a canvas pixel divided by the canvas puts the shot high. Measured at 96% too high on a fifth-of-the-screen bar.

name: FIELD-GUN19-2-the-strips-top-edge-is-dropped
note: A campaign survivor: the large HUD's bar is at the BOTTOM, so the strip starts at canvas row 0 and r.y is zero in the obvious fixture. The pin carries a strip pushed DOWN the canvas for exactly this.

name: FIELD-GUN19-3-the-rig-stops-parking-the-world-strip
note: Without the parked rect every shot is high again, with nothing else to show for it. RETRO1 re-aimed BY CONTENT: the retro mode's lines now sit beside this one; same law, same killer.

name: FIELD-GUN19-4-the-frames-strip-is-cleared-with-the-GL-state
old: this._worldViewportFrame = r ? { ...r } : null;   // FIELD-GUN19: the record, for the 2D pass
note: A getter over a field nobody assigns answers null for ever, which is the full canvas, which is the bug - and it survived a campaign that only asked whether the getter EXISTED.

name: FIELD-GUN19-5-the-blown-out-core-votes-on-hue
note: The other bug: an alpha-weighted mean of a glowing sprite is dominated by its over-exposed white core, and peak-normalising makes it paler still. The answer was a lavender indistinguishable from white.

name: FIELD-GUN19-6-the-greyscale-fallback-is-dropped
old: if (!w) { r = pr; g = pg; b = pb; w = pw; }   // nothing chromatic: the old answer, on purpose
note: The fallback is part of the rule, not a guard: a genuinely white orb must answer white rather than nothing.

name: FIELD-GUN19-7-the-peak-normalise-is-dropped
old: return [r / peak, g / peak, b / peak];
new: return [r / w, g / w, b / w];
note: This is a tint DIRECTION, not a strength - the flash curve and flashRange are already tuned, and a dim mean would darken the flash as a side effect of asking what colour it is.
